contexts.text: The worship (of the Babylonians there) consists in masses, as in the world, which are performed in a language not common to Spirits; but composed of high-sounding words, which strike a holy external and tremor; and which are not at all understood.

To prevent (the profanation of all things of the Word and of the Church) the Lord by His Divine Providence took care that they should... place holy worship in masses not understood by the common people...
Preface. Illustrated. (The doctrinals of the Roman Catholics) concerning masses, quoted.
The external affections in which they are while they are hearing masses... are merely natural, sensuous, and corporeal...

Is this not solely for the sake of masses, which they call sacrifices propitiatory, most holy, pure, with nothing but what is most holy in them; by which they infuse holiness into the bodily senses of men, and at the same time infuse night into all things of faith and spiritual life; and this for the reason that in the thick darkness they may dominate and acquire gain?
For a like reason the Roman Catholics cry out their masses in the Latin idiom...
For they... instituted Divine worship in masses not understood by the common people... Signified.
